hypothesis: A single positive whole-word nonblank retention loss restores lost wakes on unseen positives while preserving the natural-negative benefit from B13.
training_reference: Use B9 root and reproduce B13 natural-negative optimization in both arms. Require state tensors in the new same-job control to equal the archived B13 challenger. Only challenger adds the registered positive auxiliary loss.
natural_sampling: LibriSpeech dev-other, disjoint prospective rosters of 12+12 readers each with two original utterances, immutable salt ranking and clear numeric identity exclusions. Reuse frozen B13 admission rules on new originals. No outcome-based substitutions or additions.
recovery: On the same admitted original and gain, B9 completes the wake, the B13-equivalent paired control misses, and challenger completes the wake.
positive_guard: At every original and gain, retain every wake hit from B0 and the same-job control. No increase in extra wake events on a positive relative to B9 or the paired control.
ordinary_guard: Every admitted human and synthetic ordinary original at every gain has at most as many challenger events as B9 and as the paired control.
natural_guard: At 1.0 gain reduce false-event counts against B9 in at least two different human readers; natural totals at each gain must be no higher than B0.
decision: PASS requires all conditions independently on each panel. Insufficient coverage stops the study before model evaluation. A primary PASS opens the separately frozen replication once; any other outcome closes this intervention. No score-driven second coefficient, threshold search or substituting speakers. Two passes permit further locked/edge work; no offline result releases the product.
